title: Aftershift quickpatch procedures (2am sketch)
content:
Context: quick, low-risk procedures to buy time for triage after late-night incidents. Not a replacement for proper postmortem. Keep fixes minimal and reversible.

Goals:
- stabilize user-facing latency/errors within 10–30m
- avoid data-loss and reduce blast radius
- document everything in incident thread (Slack #sre-incidents)

Quick checklist (first 10 minutes):
- 1) ACK in Slack, set channel to incident mode, add on-call lead (Mateo)
- 2) Capture top metrics: p95 latency, error rate, upstream 5xxs, backend GPU queue length
  - Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/serving/runtime-overview
- 3) Confirm if scope is single-region, single-model, or global
- 4) If queries queuing > 5000 or avg latency > 3x SLO, consider immediate fallback to smaller model variant

Fast mitigations (apply one at a time):
- A) Route traffic to warm fallback pool (preferred):
  - console rollback: go to Console -> Rollouts -> active -> select service -> Switch to fallback variant (model-small-v2).
  - CLI (if console slow): rwctl routing promote --service inference-prod --variant model-small-v2 --reason "hotfix: reduce latency"
  - Note: this increases hallucination risk; inform product.

- B) Temporarily reduce max_input_length to shave token cost:
  - Edit route config: "max_input_length": 1024 -> 512 (quick edit).
  - CLI: rwctl routes update inference-prod --route-id r-12 --set max_input_length=512
  - Watch tokens/sec; roll back if user complaints spike.

- C) Turbo autoscale burst (non-blocking):
  - Apply temp capacity increase on Dedicated pools (if customer contract allows):
    aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name asg-dedicated-prod --desired-capacity 40
  - Communicate cost impact.

- D) Kill noisy workers (last resort):
  - kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=inference-worker | grep OOMKilled
  - kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-worker -n inference --field-selector=status.phase=Running 
  - Only if memory leak suspected; note PID/replica ids in incident thread.

Kubernetes quick commands (safe patterns):
- Check pod health across AZs: kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide --selector=role=frontend
- Scale down a noisy sidecar: kubectl scale deploy logging-sidecar -n inference --replicas=1
- Describe a failing pod: kubectl describe pod pod-xyz -n inference >> /tmp/pod-xyz-desc.txt (attach to Slack)

Temporary feature toggles (low-risk):
- Disable structured output validation (only if it's blocking responses): feature-toggle off structured-validator for inference-prod via Console -> Feature flags.
- Turn off expensive reranking step for search routes: rwctl feature-set inference-prod --disable rerank-step

When to escalate to SE / Infra: (add to slack with @oncall-escalate)
- Persistent 5xx > 10 minutes after fallback applied
- Errors indicating model checkpoint mismatch or corrupted weights (alerts include model checksum mismatch)
- Instance boot failures across a whole ASG or region

Notes to self (things to log while acting):
- Time of each action (UTC), who approved, CLI output, request ids for sample failing requests
- Short blameless note: e.g., "applied fallback variant to reduce p95 at 02:34 UTC; reduced max_input_length to 512 at 02:40 UTC"

Post-fix checklist (first 2 hours):
- 1) Keep fallback for at least 30 minutes after p95 < target and errors < threshold
- 2) Take a focused request sample set (20 requests) pre/post for quality check; report to product if mismatch > 10%
- 3) Open an incident ticket (JIRA-?) with timeline and artifacts (screenshots, logs, CLI outputs)

Things to avoid (late-night):
- Do not rotate keys or change KMS/HSM settings at night unless data-exfil risk is proven
- Avoid large-scale DB migrations or schema changes
- Don’t restart control plane components unless instructed by infra lead

Unresolved / TODO items (follow up next day):
- Add a safe console shortcut for promoting fallback variants (UX ask)
- Write a small script to snapshot current routing and generate rollback commands automatically
- Confirm cost-accounting label applied when we use burst capacity (who owns bill?)

Quick diagnostic snippets (copy/paste):
- Get top error traces (CloudTrace): gcloud logging read "resource.type=container AND severity>=ERROR AND labels.k8s-pod/inference" --limit 50 --project redwood-prod
- Sample failing request from prod logs: gcloud logging read "jsonPayload.request_id=\"<REQUEST_ID>\"" --limit 1
- Count queued requests across routers (internal metric): curl -sS https://metrics-api.internal/queues?env=prod | jq '.routers[].queued'

Personal notes (handy):
- If you promote fallback, ping product and UX with quick note: "Applied model-small fallback to protect latency; will revert after verification."
- Keep a tiny incident digest in Slack summary: what we changed, why, who, next steps.

End-of-shift handover template (to paste into shift notes):
- Incident ID: <ID>
- Start: <UTC time>
- Current state: e.g., stable/fallback active/ongoing
- Actions taken (timestamps): bullet list
- Next steps for morning shift: owner + ETA (e.g., "Aisha -> triage logs and revert fallback if perf stable by 08:00 UTC")
- Important artifacts: links to logs, grafana, PRs

If anything ambiguous — default to conservative (rollback small, communicate widely).

-- end --

Notes: this doc = personal pocket-runbook; convert later to formal playbook in /shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/playbooks if we keep these steps.
